When a 'Structural pass: <path>' request is read or dispatched, re-measure the named file on the current snapshot with the code-health measure. Put the fresh production-line count, longest function and the limit breached into the reading and its acceptance criteria, replacing the numbers from when it was queued. If the file is no longer over any limit, retire the request with that reason instead of dispatching it. Acceptance: (1) a test queues a structural pass, grows the file past a second limit, and shows the reading's criteria name the new count and the limit that now applies; (2) a test shows a file back under its limits makes the request retire, not dispatch; (3) fmt, clippy and test pass.

Acceptance:
- The change is made as described: Code-health structural-pass requests keep their queue-time line counts; files grow before dispatch and the split jobs are rejected or go stale
- No unrelated behavior changes; the existing tests pass
- fmt, clippy and test pass
